title: Bharat Vidhi & Civic Core
description: Indian Constitution, legal safeguards, consumer protection, police FIR procedures, and citizen helplines.

chunks.title: National Emergency Helpline Numbers
chunks.text: National Emergency Unified Helpline: 112 (Police, Fire, Ambulance). Police: 100, Fire: 101, Ambulance: 108. Women Helpline (National): 1091 and 181. National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal: 1930. Childline Helpline: 1098. Senior Citizen Helpline (Elderline): 14567. Railway Security Helpline: 139.

chunks.title: Filing a Police FIR (First Information Report)
chunks.text: Section 154 CrPC / BNSS mandates that an officer in charge of a police station must register an FIR upon information of a cognizable offence. A citizen has the legal right to receive a signed copy of the FIR immediately and free of cost. If a police station refuses to register an FIR, the complainant can send the substance of information in writing via registered post to the Superintendent of Police (SP) or file a Zero FIR at any nearby station.

chunks.title: Fundamental Rights Guaranteed by Constitution of India
chunks.text: Part III of the Indian Constitution enshrines 6 Fundamental Rights: Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22, including speech and expression), Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24), Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28), Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30), and Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32 - enabling citizens to approach Supreme Court directly via habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari).

chunks.title: Right to Information (RTI Act 2005) Process
chunks.text: Any Indian citizen can request information from a Public Authority under RTI Act 2005. Standard application fee is ₹10 (exempt for Below Poverty Line applicants). The Public Information Officer (PIO) must supply the information within 30 days. If the matter involves life or liberty of a person, information must be provided within 48 hours.

chunks.title: Consumer Protection Act 2019 Remedies
chunks.text: Under Consumer Protection Act 2019, consumers can file e-complaints via the e-Daakhil portal without needing a lawyer. District Commissions adjudicate claims up to ₹50 Lakh, State Commissions up to ₹2 Crore, and National Commission above ₹2 Crore. Covers unfair trade practices, misleading advertisements, defective goods, and deficiency in services.
